extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters and public commenters (notice-and-comment participants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and evaluating public comments on federal rulemakings, summarizing ACUS's best practices about timing, submission format, substance, and how agencies should treat comments. Useful for commenters aiming to produce comments that agencies will treat as substantive and for agency staff designing comment processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate Comment Period Length / Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the comment filed within the official comment period (and ideally in the first half to allow time for agency processing)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS recommends at least 60 days for significant regulatory actions and at least 30 days for other rulemakings. Rubric implication: A timely-filed comment is one filed within these periods; commenters benefit from filing early enough to be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow agency-specific submission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment follow any agency-specific submission guidance (formatting, length, docket reference)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should provide guidance describing what constitutes a substantive comment. A good comment follows the agency-specific guidance provided in the NPRM or on the docket (formatting, required references, length, and other procedural directions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume public posting and public scrutiny; avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Were comments drafted with the expectation they will be publicly posted and available for others to read and build upon?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should make submitted comments publicly available. Rubric implication: Comments should be drafted assuming public scrutiny—commenters can build on others' submissions and should avoid unnecessary duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a significant adverse comment (substantive challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment explain why the rule would be inappropriate, or explain why the rule would be ineffective or unacceptable without a change?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the direct final rule context, a 'significant adverse comment' is one that (a) explains why the rule would be inappropriate (challenges underlying premise or approach), OR (b) explains why the rule would be ineffective or unacceptable without a change. Such explanations make a comment more likely to be treated as substantive by agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose specific change or alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment propose a specific change rather than just expressing opposition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubric implication: Comments that propose concrete changes (specific edits, alternative approaches, or precise regulatory language) are more substantive than those that merely voice disagreement; providing alternatives increases the likelihood the agency will act on the concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge underlying premise rather than request only marginal adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment challenge the rule's underlying premise where relevant (not merely requesting marginal adjustment)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive comments may require identifying and contesting foundational assumptions or the overall approach of the rule instead of asking for small, incremental changes. Demonstrating why the premise is flawed strengthens the comment's impact.
